heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles eSUN PETG seamlessly out of the box with its direct drive extruder and 300°C stainless steel hotend, requiring no enclosure or hardened nozzle upgrades. You can reliably achieve real-world printing speeds up to 167 mm/s capped by a conservative maximum volumetric flow rate of 14 mm³/s.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent to prevent surface tearing
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Enable Z-Hop during retraction (0.4 mm Normal) and activate 'Avoid Crossing Walls' to eliminate PETG nozzle buildup and surface dragging.
Configure nozzle temperature to 240°C for all layers and set the heatbed to 75°C for optimal layer adhesion without warping.
Reduce aux/cooling fan threshold: set Part Cooling Fan between 20% and 50% max, keeping the fan off for the first 3 layers to ensure maximum interlayer bonding.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe fine stringing and web-like hairs across open travels
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is inherently hygroscopic and fluid at 240°C, causing ooze when exposed to ambient moisture.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 hours in a filament dryer, and set OrcaSlicer wipe distance to 2.0 mm on loop.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Build plate damage or chunks torn from PEI sheet upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically bonds aggressively to smooth or bare PEI surfaces when directly printed without an interface layer.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVA glue stick or Bambu Liquid Glue as a sacrificial release agent, and wait until the bed cools to under 30°C before flexing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough, matte surface finish and brittle layer separation
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Volumetric speed exceeding 14 mm³/s causing hotend under-temperature and under-extrusion at high linear speeds.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Cap the filament profile Max Volumetric Speed at 14 mm³/s and lower outer wall speed to 120 mm/s.

faq.question: Can I print eSUN PETG on the Bambu Lab A1 without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG does not require a heated enclosure and prints reliably on the open-frame A1, provided the room is free from strong cold drafts.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for standard eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: No, standard eSUN PETG is non-abrasive, making the stock stainless steel nozzle on the Bambu Lab A1 completely sufficient.

faq.question: Why is my PETG sticking too well to the Bambu Textured PEI plate?
faq.answer: PETG has very high chemical affinity for PEI; always use a thin coat of glue stick as a release barrier to avoid stripping the PEI coating.

faq.question: What is the true maximum speed I can print eSUN PETG on the A1?
faq.answer: While the A1 can move up to 500 mm/s, eSUN PETG is limited by melting capacity to 14 mm³/s, yielding a safe maximum print speed of 167 mm/s at 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width.
